scenario: Floa local video selection, playback, and resume persistence

fixture.generation: Repeated the repository's existing 7.5 second MP4 eight times using AVFoundation; no Glaso assets were used.

steps.action: Open Local Video using Option+Command+O and select the MP4 in the macOS picker
steps.observation: The picker showed the fixture and opened a separate Floa local video window.

steps.action: Start playback in the player controls
steps.observation: The accessible Play button changed to Pause. The decoded frame and playback controls were visible in the player.

steps.action: Seek to 30 seconds and allow the player IPC to save the seeked position
steps.observation: The player showed 0:30; isolated browser-data.json stored time=30 with matching file size and modification timestamp. Seeking was set through CDP for deterministic positioning; the actual player seeked handler and IPC persisted it.

steps.action: Close the player window, reopen the same file from the native picker, and inspect playback
steps.observation: The reopened player had duration=60, currentTime=39.4898, paused=false, and readyState=4. It had resumed from the stored 30 second position and continued playing before observation.

steps.action: Check playback with Floa obscured in an isolated renderer probe
steps.observation: The main browser document became hidden during the probe and playback stopped. The dedicated media BrowserWindow now sets backgroundThrottling=false; the successful end-to-end player above reported visibility=visible.

limitations: Volume and mute changes were not included in this scenario.

Position setting was deterministic CDP input rather than dragging the native time scrubber. The player seeked event, IPC save, app profile persistence, native reopen, and resumed playback were exercised.
